relatedSnapshot.title: Master: unpaid mailboxes from a refunded DFY order cannot be paid from the billing page
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The billing page cannot take payment for mailboxes that the platform still bills the provider for. When a Done-For-You domain order is refunded because the provider failed to provision it, the mailboxes it created are still live and in use, the audit flags them unpaid and warns they will be cancelled on a dated deadline, and the resubscribe control that would settle them never renders. Customers see a warning they cannot act on, and the mailboxes are removed while they are willing to pay.

## Problem

An owner opens Settings -> Billing from the "Review billing" banner, expecting to pay for the mailboxes the banner names. The page shows no managed domains for that workspace, so there is no "Review and resubscribe" and no per-domain "Resubscribe", and no other surface opens the pay dialog. Support then tells the customer a payment failed, when the only inbox charge was refunded.

## Root cause

`apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts` `listManagedDomains` inner-joins the domain's purchase order and filters `ne(domainPurchaseOrderTable.status, 'refunded')` (and `ne(mailDomainTable.status, 'suspended')`). A refunded order therefore removes its domain from the managed list even while an open unpaid audit finding exists for it. `apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx` `EmailAccountsDomainsCard` returns its "No managed domains" empty state before rendering the "Review and resubscribe" and per-domain "Resubscribe" buttons, and those are the only entry points to the pay flow (`apps/web/trpc/routers/cmr-domain-charges.ts` `listUnpaid` already returns the domain for an owner or admin, regardless of order status). When the card does render for a workspace with other domains, the refunded domain is still hidden from the list, so its per-domain control is missing too.

## Blast radius

Counted 2026-10-05 against production. 4 organizations and 9 open `unpaid` findings belong to a refunded purchase order; 2 of those organizations have an empty managed list, where the control is unreachable (6 findings), and the other 2 keep 3 and 4 visible managed domains, where only the per-domain control is missing (3 findings). All 4 organizations have a sent unpaid reminder dated 2026-09-29, so all 4 face a 2026-10-06 cancellation date. Distinct affected users were not counted: the audit rows carry no user id.

```
WITH f AS (SELECT fa.organization_id FROM cmr_domain_audit_finding fa
  JOIN domain_purchase_order o ON o.id = fa.order_id
  WHERE fa.payment_state = 'unpaid' AND fa.resolved_at IS NULL
    AND fa.dismissed_at IS NULL AND o.status = 'refunded')
SELECT f.organization_id::text, count(*) AS open_findings,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM mail_domain md
     JOIN domain_purchase_order o2 ON o2.id = md.order_id
    WHERE md.organization_id = f.organization_id
      AND md.status <> 'suspended' AND o2.status <> 'refunded') AS visible_managed_domains,
  (SELECT min(r.created_at)::text FROM cmr_renewal_reminder r
    WHERE r.organization_id = f.organization_id
      AND r.kind = 'unpaid' AND r.status = 'sent') AS first_sent_reminder
FROM f GROUP BY f.organization_id
```

Confirmed affected: 2 organizations with the control unreachable. Potentially exposed: the further 2 organizations whose refunded domain is hidden from the list while their pay-all control is reachable.

## Proposed fix

Make the unpaid-mailbox notice actionable for every workspace that carries an open unpaid finding. A workspace whose DFY order was refunded but whose provider mailboxes are still live should be able to pay for them from the billing page: the pay control should be reachable from the unpaid findings themselves rather than only from the managed domain list, and a refunded order's domain should stay visible to the billing card while an open unpaid finding exists so its per-domain "Resubscribe" renders as well. The customer-facing outcome is that the banner's deadline can be met from the billing page, without an operator making a production or billing change by hand.

## What's included

Both variants found in the blast radius (empty card, and refunded domain hidden beside visible ones). Not included: the upstream provisioning failure that leaves mailboxes live after a refunded order (owned by the DFY provisioning family tracked under ENG-13213), and the wording of the reminder emails. Related umbrella work: ENG-13358, whose child ENG-14423 covers giving customers a clear date to act by. Separately filed work needed for the current cohort: an operator must make the affected mailboxes payable, or decide they are removed, before 2026-10-06.

## Regression seam

The billing page's managed-domain list and its pay control. Red before: for a workspace whose only mail domain belongs to a refunded order while an open unpaid finding exists, `listManagedDomains` returns nothing and the billing card renders its empty state with no pay control. Green after: the same workspace offers a working resubscribe path that charges for the live mailboxes and clears the finding.

## Done when

* An owner of a workspace whose DFY order was refunded but whose provider mailboxes are live can open Settings -> Billing and pay for those mailboxes from the page.
* A workspace that also has other managed domains shows the per-domain resubscribe control for the refunded domain while its unpaid finding is open.
* A regression test at the list/pay seam proves both cases red before and green after.

## Reports

* ENG-14710 (customer report, Company One workspace; carries the full investigation document).

relatedSnapshot.title: Charged twice for the same domain and inbox bundle; one bundle was never delivered and its subscription is still billing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: customer-initiated Intercom conversation, opened 2026-09-30, contact Name 14 <email>, workspace "Name 15 Workspace", owner role. Initial message: "I have a billing issue that isn't being sorted. Please escalate to someone asap!" Asked for detail: "I've been billed twice for emails and domains for the last 3 months when that's not what I'm using." Declined the self-serve answer: "No, I still need help." No attachments.

Bucket: overcharged.

Finding: the customer bought the same DFY bundle (1 domain + 3 inboxes) twice about 17 hours apart and was charged for both; only one bundle was ever delivered. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-23 14:01Z) was cancelled for "Payment timeout - order automatically cancelled after 30 minutes" with nothing provisioned, but its Autumn subscription and its Stripe charges landed anyway. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-24 06:47Z) completed and is the bundle the customer actually uses (3 active connected inboxes). The cancelled order's subscription was never cancelled, so it has kept invoicing every month since.

Exposure (Stripe, smallest currency unit, all succeeded and unrefunded, no credit notes):

* 2026-07-23, 3276 cents ($32.76), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0017
* 2026-08-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0021
* 2026-09-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0025
  Total already collected for the undelivered bundle: $68.76, and $18.00/month continues until the orphan subscription is cancelled. The delivered bundle's own charges are legitimate and are not part of this ask.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise): refund the $68.76 collected for the undelivered bundle, and cancel the orphan domain and inbox line items on the billing account so the recurring $18.00/month stops. A Stripe customer credit is the alternative if the customer would rather have it applied forward (the Legacy Pro plan bills monthly, so there is a future invoice to consume it). The customer has not yet said which they want. No money has been moved and nothing has been cancelled.

Full readout, systems of record, and the code path are in the Billing investigation document on this ticket.
